blocks.label: The sixteen towns problem
blocks.html:
The problem I see most

Why does your site list sixteen towns but ring from one?

Most service sites put every town they cover on one page. To Google, that is one page about everything. It can rank for one place. The other fifteen towns go to whoever gave Google a page for them.

  • 01
    One page, many places. A list of towns is not a reason to rank in any of them.
  • 02
    Each town needs its own page. Its own services, questions, proof and links.
  • 03
    Structure before content. More blog posts will not fix a site Google cannot read.
Pages that can rank:1

blocks.label: Method
blocks.html:
The method

How does semantic SEO turn a website into a system?

I trained as a mechanical engineer. I build sites the way I was taught to build machines. Every part has one job, and every part connects. This is the Koray Tuğberk Gübür framework, applied step by step.

01

Source Context

Who you are, what you sell, and why Google should trust you on it.

02

Central Entity

The one thing the whole site is about. Every page points back to it.

03

Topical Map

Every service, town and question mapped into core and outer sections.

04

Content Briefs

Headings, questions and anchor texts set before a word is written.

05

Semantic Content

Clear answers in plain words, written for owners and for search engines.

06

Configuration

Internal links, schema, speed and indexing. The wiring of the machine.

07

Measure

Calls, quote requests, booked jobs and sales. That is the scoreboard.

blocks.label: What Google reads
blocks.html:
Why the layout matters

What has Google said about how it reads a page?

We build to what Google has patented and said in public. We don't sell any of it as a guaranteed ranking factor. We use it to make pages cheaper for Google to read and easier for owners' customers to use.

US Patent 12393768

Layout-aware multimodal document understanding

Google describes reading a page as blocks of text, image, table and layout, then how those blocks relate.

So block order and structure carry meaning.
US 10824630 · US 11238058

Structured information cards

Repeated cards with labels, values and an entity can trigger a card template in search.

So service and price cards get the same structure every time.
Martin Splitt, Google, 2021

Centerpiece annotation

Google finds the main content block of a page and gives boilerplate around it less weight.

So the answer goes first, before badges and banners.
Pandu Nayak, DOJ trial testimony

Cheap signals first

Google runs fast topicality checks before its expensive ranking systems look at a shortlist.

So a page that is hard to read can drop out early.
((Historical data × Topical coverage) ÷ Cost of retrieval) × Right visual annotations

Koray Tuğberk Gübür's topical authority formula. Visual annotations are a multiplier. Get the layout wrong and everything above it is multiplied by close to zero. That is why we plan SEO and design as one job.

blocks.label: Process
blocks.html:
Working together

What happens after you book a call?

No long contracts before you see the plan. Four phases, each with something you can check.

Phase 1

The call

Thirty minutes. I show you how Google reads your site today, and you tell me what a good month looks like for you.

Phase 2

The map

Source context, central entity and a topical map. You see every page before we build any of them.

Phase 3

The build

Pages, content, schema and internal links go live in the order the map sets, core sections first.

Phase 4

The growth

New nodes added as Google trusts the site more. Reports in calls, quotes and booked jobs.

What do we measure?

Rankings are a means, not the result. You count the phone, so I do too. New town pages take a few months to start ringing. I tell you that before we talk about any number.
